name: Solution Delivery
description: An end-to-end software delivery engagement: frame the problem and baseline the requirements, design the architecture and the detail, plan and specify the build, then define how the solution is verified and judged ready to release.
principles: Design decisions are recorded with their alternatives and their trade-offs, not just their conclusions.
Non-functional requirements are design inputs, not late discoveries.
Slice work so that each increment is independently valuable and independently testable.
Test effort follows risk, not uniform coverage.
Reversible decisions are made fast; irreversible ones are made deliberately.
Nothing is 'done' without agreed, observable acceptance criteria.

stages.name: Discovery
stages.description: Frame the problem, bound the scope, and baseline what the solution must do before any design work begins.

quality_gate.description: Discovery is complete when the problem, scope and success measures are agreed and the requirements baseline is testable.

deliverables.name: Solution Brief
deliverables.description: The problem being solved, who it is being solved for, what is in and out of scope, and how success will be judged.

activities.name: Frame the problem
activities.description: State the problem in business terms with its cost and its affected parties, and identify the sponsor and the decision-makers for the delivery.

activities.name: Define scope and success measures
activities.description: Bound what is in and explicitly out of scope, and define the measurable outcomes that will determine whether the delivery succeeded.

deliverables.name: Requirements Baseline
deliverables.description: The agreed functional and non-functional requirements and the stories that carry them into delivery.

activities.name: Elicit requirements
activities.description: Produce identified, prioritised, verifiable functional and non-functional requirements, with assumptions, constraints and open questions recorded.

activities.name: Write delivery stories
activities.description: Slice the requirements into vertically sliced, INVEST-compliant stories grouped into epics and prioritised for delivery sequencing.

stages.name: Design
stages.description: Choose and record the target architecture, then take it down to the component, domain and interface detail a team can build from.

quality_gate.description: Design is complete when the architecture decision is recorded with its alternatives, the domain and interfaces are specified, and the delivery risks are owned.

deliverables.name: Solution Architecture
deliverables.description: The target architecture, the options rejected in reaching it, and the risks it carries.

activities.name: Evaluate architecture options
activities.description: Score at least three viable architectural approaches against weighted criteria derived from the requirements, and recommend one with its trade-offs stated.

activities.name: Define the target architecture
activities.description: Describe the components, their responsibilities, the data flows between them and how the non-functional requirements are satisfied by the design.

activities.name: Assess delivery risks
activities.description: Produce a ranked risk register covering dependency, data, capability, adoption and third-party risk, each with an owner, treatment and residual rating.

deliverables.name: Detailed Design
deliverables.description: The domain model, component design and interface contracts the build will implement.

activities.name: Model the domain
activities.description: Define the entities, relationships, invariants, lifecycles and business rules in the language of the business, with a glossary of terms.

activities.name: Specify interfaces and contracts
activities.description: Define each interface between components and to external systems: operations, payloads, errors, idempotency, versioning and the failure behaviour on each side.

stages.name: Build
stages.description: Sequence the implementation into increments, specify how each component is to be built, and agree what done means before work starts.

quality_gate.description: Build planning is complete when the increments are sequenced against real dependencies, each component has an implementation specification, and the definition of done is agreed.

deliverables.name: Implementation Plan
deliverables.description: How the solution is built: the increments, their order, the component-level specifications, and the definition of done.

activities.name: Plan implementation increments
activities.description: Break the build into increments that each end in something demonstrable, showing hard dependencies separately from convenient ordering.

activities.name: Specify component implementation
activities.description: For each component, state its responsibilities, its collaborators, the patterns and libraries to be used, its error handling and its observability requirements.

activities.name: Define done criteria
activities.description: Agree the definition of done for an increment — tests, review, documentation, non-functional thresholds — and the acceptance criteria for the priority stories.

stages.name: Test
stages.description: Define how the solution is verified and validated, design the tests that carry the most risk, and judge release readiness.

quality_gate.description: Test is complete when the strategy is risk-based with stated exit criteria, the priority scenarios are designed, and a readiness recommendation with residual risk is on record.

deliverables.name: Test Strategy and Plan
deliverables.description: What is tested, at which level, in what environment, with what data, and against what exit criteria.

activities.name: Define the test strategy
activities.description: Set the levels, ownership, environments, data approach, defect triage and release exit criteria, concentrating effort where production failure would be most damaging.

activities.name: Design test scenarios
activities.description: Write executable Given/When/Then scenarios for the priority stories covering happy path, boundaries, invalid input, permissions and dependency failure.

deliverables.name: Release Readiness Assessment
deliverables.description: Whether the solution should go live, on what evidence, and with what residual risk accepted.

activities.name: Assess release readiness
activities.description: Judge readiness against the exit criteria, list open defects and coverage gaps by severity, and give a go, no-go or conditional recommendation with the residual risks named and owned.
